steps.text: Part 2 of 4: Ways a game is drawn. This part covers The fifty-move clock. Each part is short on purpose: finish one, play a game or take a break, and come back.

The second way to a draw is **no progress**. Count in **half-moves**: one move by one player is one half-move. The count goes back to zero after any capture or any pawn move, because those change the game for good. When it reaches 100, which is fifty moves by each player, a player may claim a draw. This is the **fifty-move rule**.

steps.title: Does the clock go back to zero?

steps.caption: Nothing is captured and no pawn moves, so every half-move adds one to the count. Say the clock aloud as you step.

line.say: Clock 4. Even a changing position adds to the count when nothing is captured and no pawn moves.

claims.statement: The rook can step to a2.

steps.caption: The clock shows 40 here. Both kings walk, then the rook takes a loose pawn. Watch what the capture does to the count.

line.say: The rook takes the unprotected pawn. The count goes back to 0.

claims.statement: After the capture the rook stands on a5.
The king can step to d2.

steps.caption: The clock shows 0 after the capture. Black to move. A check is coming; does it reset the count?

line.say: The rook gives check. Clock 4: a check does not reset the count.

claims.statement: After the last move the black king on f6 is attacked, so it is a check.

steps.caption: The clock shows 30. Now a pawn moves. Watch the count.

line.say: A pawn move. The count goes back to 0.
The rook moves. Clock 4. Only the pawn move reset the count; nothing since has.

claims.statement: The pawn can advance to a4.
After the move the pawn stands on a4.

steps.text: At 100 half-moves a player whose turn it is **may** claim the draw. Until someone claims, play goes on. The player who is ahead may well prefer to play on. [S] At 150 half-moves the game ends without a claim, unless the last move is checkmate. A rules library agrees; a human reviewer still has to check the printed Laws.

**Claiming and agreeing.** To claim, you tell the arbiter or press the claim button on a screen. For agreement, one player offers and the other must accept; a declined offer changes nothing. [R] Details differ by event, and a reviewer is to check them against Article 9.

**Remember.** The fifty-move rule counts half-moves, one move by one player each. Any capture or pawn move sets the count back to zero; a check does not. At 100, the player to move may claim a draw, but until someone claims, play goes on. The player who is ahead may prefer to keep playing.
